messages:
maria-ops: Heads-up: AZ8 thermal sensors spiked last night. We're scheduling a preemptive maintenance window to swap node cohorts and do warm reboots to avoid throttling. Window: Mon 2025-06-23 02:00–06:00 UTC. Expected impact: ~18% GPU capacity reduction in AZ8 for ~60m per cohort as we cycle groups. Will try to keep Dedicated pools at SLO via cross-region routing.

oliver-sre: Thanks — what's the cohort size and how many cohorts?

maria-ops: Cohorts are 25 nodes (~200 GPUs) each, 3 cohorts total. We'll cordon+drain one cohort at a time, then warm-restart and verify telemetry before uncordoning. Sequence: cordon -> drain (evict long jobs) -> reboot -> kernel microcode check -> uncordon -> warmup KV cache.

tim-infra: Quick note: for Dedicated customers we should avoid mass evictions. Can we shift steady-state traffic to AZ5 for the 4-hour window? Region capacity permits ~30% short-term absorb.

anna-ml: Will there be any model-serving cache flushes? We rely on prefix cache for latency-critical models. Need ETA on warmup time.

maria-ops: Good point. Plan is to run prefix cache prewarm script during uncordon. Expect ~10–15m warmup for the hot model set per cohort. I'll attach the command we run:
```bash
# drain + eviction
kubectl cordon node-xyz
kubectl drain node-xyz --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
# post-reboot healthcheck (pseudo)
curl -s http://node-xyz:8080/health | jq .
```

deploy-bot: [deploy-scheduler] Scheduled maintenance job id=maint-az8-246; cohort=1 at 2025-06-23T02:10:00Z.

oliver-sre: Who's owning the fallback routing? We should set a temporary policy to route new requests out-of-region rather than queue when local GPU queues back up.

maria-ops: @oliver-sre I'll own routing changes. Plan: update smart-routing policy to prefer AZ5/AZ2 for 60m during cohort operations, fallback to cheaper model variant only if cross-region saturates.

sre-oncall: Please add a health-check escalation if token latency  p50 > 250ms or error rate > 1% for 5m. I'll keep pager muted unless thresholds hit.

tim-infra: Cost callout: cross-region routing will increase egress and inter-region provisioning spend. Suggest enabling short-lived spot backfill in AZ8 for background batch jobs so we don't blow reserved capacity costs.

maria-ops: Agreed — we'll shift non-critical spot workloads into a backfill queue and set priority=low. Can we tag the backfill jobs with `maintenance:az8-2025-06-23` for chargeback?

anna-ml: One more ask — please don't rotate nodes hosting the AB test for the new quantized model until after cohort 2 completes. We need stable latency during the experiment window.

maria-ops: Noted. We'll pin the canary tasks to surviving cohorts and add a guard to skip nodes with label `abtest=quant-v2`.

oliver-sre: Can someone update the Redwood Console banner + status page copy? Users should see a short blurb pointing at the maintenance FAQ and a link to realtime health: https://status.redwood.ai/az8?utm=maintenance

sre-oncall: I'll post a brief public-facing banner at T-2h and a follow-up at start and end.

maria-ops: Final checklist for cohort run (copying here):
- Reserve warm spare pool in AZ5 (30% headroom)
- Push routing policy change (60m scope)
- Backfill non-critical jobs to spot queue
- Protect AB test pods via nodeLabel
- Run prefix-cache warmup after uncordon
- Pager thresholds set by @sre-oncall

maria-ops: If no objections, we'll kick cohort-1 Monday 02:10 UTC. Post any blockers here by EOD today. :thumbsup:

oliver-sre: :thumbsup: looks good from infra side.

tim-infra: Approved. Will monitor costs and adjust if egress spikes.

anna-ml: Approved from ML side, thanks for the heads-up.

sre-oncall: Acknowledged. Oncall will monitor the runbooks and escalate if health thresholds cross.
